initiatives.name: Secure construction
initiatives.description: Prevent vulnerability classes through enforceable architectural constraints (typed database access, no user HTML, no application JavaScript outside Limen, memory-safe languages, deny-by-default authorization).
initiatives.origin: Initiative register baseline 2026-11-25; Secure Construction Standard v0.1.
initiatives.rationale: Removing whole defect classes by construction is cheaper and more reliable than finding instances later.
initiatives.problem: Scanning and review find instances of known weakness classes but do not prevent recurrence.
intendedOutcomes: Each SEC-* rule has an owner, enforcement mechanism, negative tests and evidence
Unbound is the first product built under the standard
successCriteria: Every mandatory SEC-* rule has machine-checkable enforcement and a passing negative test suite
Scanner validation report published per scanner release
evidence: tutela repository: security engineering discipline and secret scanning (tutela-foundation.yml)
outstandingDecisions: Formal adoption of the Secure Construction Standard
Whether Tutela or Aegis owns the rule registry (the standard names Aegis; Tutela's charter describes security invariants and controls)
risks: Rule ownership is split between Aegis (named in the standard) and Tutela (security discipline), risking duplicated rule registries
Claims of eliminated vulnerability classes without scoped evidence
nextActions: Translate the standard into verifiable requirements with one owner per rule
completionCriteria: All mandatory rules enforced fail-closed in Unbound CI with evidence

initiatives.name: Customer due diligence
initiatives.description: Anticipate enterprise and financial-institution due diligence questions and answer them from evidence-backed, reusable records.
initiatives.rationale: Questionnaire effort and procurement delay are recurring costs; reusable evidence-backed answers reduce them.
initiatives.problem: Each questionnaire is answered from scratch and answers drift from reality.
intendedOutcomes: Canonical question bank with target and approved current answers
Answers carry claim status, scope and evidence references
successCriteria: Share of questionnaire questions answered from approved records (metric M-12) measured on the first real questionnaire
evidence: echelon-due-diligence research branch established 2026-11-25 (Praxis installed, taxonomy)
outstandingDecisions: Licensing of standard questionnaire content (SIG, CAIQ) before storing question text
risks: Publishing answers that overstate implementation (claim discipline mitigates)
nextActions: Continue the comprehensive due diligence research initiative
Adopt the claim status vocabulary of POL-ORG-TRN-001 §6
completionCriteria: First real customer questionnaire answered from approved records with measured effort

initiatives.name: Continuous compliance
initiatives.description: Generate current assurance evidence during normal engineering and operations instead of periodic collection.
initiatives.rationale: Evidence produced as a by-product is cheaper, fresher and harder to fabricate than evidence assembled for an audit.
initiatives.problem: Periodic evidence collection is expensive and goes stale between assessments.
intendedOutcomes: Evidence with provenance, freshness, expiry and revocation
successCriteria: Percentage of controls with current automatically generated evidence (metrics M-10, M-13)
evidence: echelon-assurance research branch (control catalog, evidence architecture, integration assessment) — unmerged as of 2026-11-25
outstandingDecisions: echelon-assurance repository visibility: owner directed private, observed public (OD-GOV-002)
Enable Praxis verified/attested completion in repositories (implemented but not enabled per the assurance integration assessment)
risks: Internal verification misrepresented as independent assurance
Self-reported provenance treated as authenticated
nextActions: Merge or reconcile the assurance research branch
Enable verified completion in one pilot repository
completionCriteria: Unbound control set has continuously generated, fresh evidence for each automated control
